gaussian_question.:question/problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ for the variables $x,y,z$ in that order.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}-2 & -4 & -4 & 4 \\ -1 & -2 & -5 & -1 \\ -2 & -2 & 0 & -4\end{array}\right]
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix to row echelon form. Select the resulting augmented matrix.
gaussian_question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix is

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}-2 & -4 & -4 & 4 \\ -1 & -2 & -5 & -1 \\ -2 & -2 & 0 & -4\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize the first pivot with $R_1:=-\frac{1}{2}R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 2 & -2 \\ -1 & -2 & -5 & -1 \\ -2 & -2 & 0 & -4\end{array}\right]
$$

$R_2:=R_2+(1)R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 2 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & -3 & -3 \\ -2 & -2 & 0 & -4\end{array}\right]
$$

$R_3:=R_3+(2)R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 2 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & -3 & -3 \\ 0 & 2 & 4 & -8\end{array}\right]
$$

The second pivot is zero, while the third row has a nonzero second entry. Exchange $R_2$ and $R_3$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 2 & -2 \\ 0 & 2 & 4 & -8 \\ 0 & 0 & -3 & -3\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize with $R_2:=\frac{1}{2}R_2$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 2 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & -3 & -3\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize with $R_3:=-\frac{1}{3}R_3$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 2 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{array}\right]
$$

Thus the row echelon matrix is

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 2 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{array}\right]
$$
